_: Copy to cloudflare/access.json (gitignored) and fill in. Desired state for the PRIVATE tunnel. Apply with cloudflare/apply.sh. JSON, not YAML, because no python on the admin box or the host has PyYAML and this script stays stdlib-only. The long-form reasoning lives in cloudflare/README.md; each entry's `why` is the short version.

tunnel.name: homelab-private
tunnel.why: Locally managed so ingress rules live in cloudflare/ingress.yml in this repo rather than in the dashboard. Costs a credentials JSON instead of a TUNNEL_TOKEN.

hostnames.name: d
hostnames.why: Den Web. Browsers can render an Access login, so it gets one.

hostnames.name: d-scout
hostnames.why: scout JSON API. Bypassed it becomes a free public aggregator: a stranger mints their own install, and the scraping leaves from the home IP, so the indexers rate-limit and blocklist YOU.

hostnames.name: d-subs
hostnames.why: den-subtitles JSON API. Bypassed it becomes a public subtitle proxy running audio sync on the box's CPU.

hostnames.name: d-api
hostnames.why: den-edge device API. Built as an untrusted relay and authorises each request itself. A TV cannot render a login page, and a service token cannot bootstrap: a factory-reset TV has no token and must reach den-edge to be given one.

hostnames.name: d-play
hostnames.why: scout play tickets ONLY. Separate host because the TV plays /p/<ticket> directly and scout 302s to the debrid; players repeat custom headers across redirects, so an Access token would reach the debrid's CDN on every play. A ticket is its own authority: one release, 24h. The allowlist fails closed.

_not_exposed: den-reel and den-remux are absent on purpose. They serve video, and Cloudflare's terms restrict serving video through the CDN/Tunnel outside Stream/R2. Both stay LAN + tailnet; a remote TV falls back to YouTube trailers. Do not add them here.

service_tokens.name: den-tv
service_tokens.why: Non-identity credential the TVs send as CF-Access-Client-*. Delivered through den-edge's library log (set:keys) so it rotates without an app release, and it lives ONLY on the TVs.

rate_limits.description: den-edge /pair: cap online guessing against CPace
rate_limits.why: /pair is internet-facing and outside Access, so CPace's resistance to ONLINE guessing rests on den-edge's own attempt cap. WAF rules still apply to Access-bypassed paths. FREE PLAN: period and mitigation_timeout must both be 10 and there is one rule per zone — the API rejects anything else with 'not entitled'.
